day_shape: Southern Lebanon escalation dominates: IDF confirms killing two Hezbollah commanders (Abu Hassan Alaa, Ali Samir Al-Haj Hassan) after a drone attack seriously wounded three soldiers at Ali Taher Ridge, Iran executes Karaj protester Shahram Sadeqi, third reported Iran attack on a UAE-flagged tanker in the Strait of Hormuz.

threads.label: Southern Lebanon strikes and Hezbollah commanders killed
threads.summary: The IDF confirmed killing Hezbollah battalion commander Ali Samir Al-Haj Hassan in Ansar and Badder Unit commander Abu Hassan Alaa in Deir al-Zahrani after a Hezbollah explosive drone at Ali Taher Ridge seriously wounded three Yahalom soldiers. Lebanese media reported seven killed in Ansar; President Joseph Aoun condemned the strikes as a framework-agreement violation, and Upper Galilee residents were warned of overnight artillery and airstrikes.

threads.label: Karaj death-car execution
threads.summary: Iran executed Shahram Sadeqi on Sunday morning over a January 8 incident in which a Peugeot 405 ran over officials at Golzar junction in Karaj during protests. State outlets described the charges as operational activity for Israel and the United States, while Iran International framed it as a protest-linked execution reported by judiciary outlet Mizan.

threads.label: Strait of Hormuz tanker attack and naval posture
threads.summary: The Jerusalem Post reported an Abu Dhabi National Oil Company vessel was attacked by Iran in the Strait of Hormuz — the third such incident in a week — with the UAE calling for attacks to stop. CENTCOM posted imagery of USS George H.W. Bush operating in the Arabian Sea, and Iran's parliament is reviewing a smart-management plan for the Strait.

threads.label: Iranian pilots held in Qatar dispute
threads.summary: Iran International reported three Iranian Su-24 pilots had been held in Qatar for six months after being captured by Qatari forces. Qatar rejected the claim on Saturday, saying it recovered only one pilot's remains and had invited Tehran to review the search.

threads.label: Iran domestic pressure, legislation and oil network
threads.summary: Iran International reported nine people tied to an $11-billion oil-sales network, including Mohsen Rezaei's son, and separately that Iranian authorities are turning to potential domestic unrest. IRIB said parliament will finalise a bill criminalising international war crimes and a foreign infiltration plan; Iran International also reported non-oil trade down around 30% since the war.

threads.label: Gaza operations and Hamas Cairo talks
threads.summary: The IDF said a Givati Brigade tank was struck by a Hamas explosive device near the Yellow Line in southern Gaza with no injuries, and Paratroopers spotted operatives crossing the line. The Jerusalem Post reported a Hamas delegation was expected in Cairo Sunday to discuss the 15-point Board of Peace plan for Gaza.

threads.label: Regime messaging on war and IRGC leadership
threads.summary: Khamenei's office published an excerpt from the decree appointing General Ahmad Vahidi as IRGC Commander-in-Chief, framing the system as in strategic confrontation with global arrogance. Defa Press posted an "asymmetric epic" retrospective on the 40-day war citing AirWars figures, and the Jerusalem Post reported Speaker Ghalibaf claimed contact with Hezbollah despite Lebanese objections.

events.summary_en: Russia: Ukraine lost 1.75 billion dollars in export revenue due to port closure. Russia announced that Ukraine has lost approximately 1.75 billion dollars in export revenues since 22 July due to the closure of maritime ports. According to the Russian TASS news agency; Ukraine's three major commercial ports including Odesa, Chornomorsk and Yuzhne have not been in operation. Data on ship transit schedules shows that during this period, no large foreign commercial vessels have entered these ports.

events.summary_en: Driver of death car at Golzar junction in Karaj executed. On the evening of 18 Dey last year and during the American-Zionist coup, Shahram Sadeqi near Golzar junction in Karaj, after attacking officials with a Peugeot 405 car known as the death car, ran over several officials and caused severe injuries to seven FRAJ officials. One of the officials injured at this scene was in a coma for 3 months. Sadeqi, who fled the scene after this brutal attack by setting his car on fire, was identified, arrested, tried and hanged this morning.

events.summary_en: Heavy losses to Pakistan's fishing and boat-building industry in Iran's regional war. Iran's regional war has faced Pakistan's tuna trade, a significant portion of which is dependent on the Iranian market, with a serious crisis and affected the activity of thousands of fishermen and this country's boat-building industry. Tuna holds a special place in Iran's food basket, but its consumption in Pakistan is limited and Pakistani fishermen have limited options for selling their catch. For this reason, the Iranian market has become one of the most important destinations for tuna caught in Pakistani waters in recent years.

events.summary_en: Poor performance of Ukrainian Flamingo missiles. Long-range 'Flamingo' missiles, which were supposed to change the equations of the Ukraine war, did not perform acceptably on Russian soil. On 17 Tir, the Ukrainian army attacked Russia with five Flamingo cruise missiles, all of which were shot down by Russia's air defence system. These missiles were launched from the Sumy and Chernihiv regions and were shot down by Russian air defences in the Tambov and Penza areas, at distances of approximately 430 and 630 kilometres from the Ukrainian border.

According to this report, Ukraine's situation before winter is so fragile that Zelensky has not only asked his diplomats to issue warnings around the world, but has personally appealed as well. According to the newspaper, his pleas for help are a sign of desperation, because there is a shortage of air defence missiles worldwide and Europeans and Americans are also facing shortages of it.

events.title_en: Europe's gas reserves depleted. The European Gas Infrastructure Organisation reported that the level of gas storage in Europe's underground facilities is at its lowest level in the past 5 years.
events.summary_en: Europe's gas reserves depleted. The European Gas Infrastructure Organisation reported that the level of gas storage in Europe's underground facilities is at its lowest level in the past 5 years. Following the start of the Russia-Ukraine war, European countries lost one of their primary sources of gas supply, and now the crisis in the Strait of Hormuz has disrupted imports of Qatari gas.

events.title: The three soldiers who were seriously wounded in southern Lebanon overnight were hit by an explosive drone launched by Hezbollah, according to the military. At around 2:30 a.m., Hezbollah launched the drone at troops operating at the Ali Taher Ridge area. The drone exploded near soldiers of the elite Yahalom combat engineering unit, seriously wounding an officer and two soldiers. The soldiers were taken to a hospital and their families were notified, the army adds. In response, the military struck Hezbollah sites in Nabatieh and Ansar, killing a senior commander in the terror group.
